chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عِمْرَانَ، الْمَخْزُومِيُّ، الْمُلَقَّبُ بِالْمَيْمُونِ. كَانَ غَالِيًا. ضَعِيفًا.

translations.en: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn 'Imran, al-Makhzumi, the one who has the laqab of “al-Maymun”. He was a ghali. Weak.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Ali ibn Abdullah as a *ghali* (exaggerator), a category of narrators whose theological excesses often led to their rejection in hadith criticism despite their reliability in transmission. His designation as *da'if* highlights the Shia scholarly practice of linking theological accuracy—specifically avoiding divine attributes or excessive veneration of the Imams—to the validity of one's narrations. This reflects the broader tradition of evaluating narrators not just on memory, but on their adherence to orthodox Twelver doctrine.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Abdullah al-Maymun and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالِيًا: ghali; one who exaggerates in the virtues or divinity of the Imams
key_terms.ضَعِيفًا: da'if; weak; having a lower grade of reliability in hadith transmission
